metadata.case_name: LAM KAN MAU v. WIN CAPITAL (HK) LTD AND OTHERS

injuries.description: Multiple facial lacerations with active bleeding over the left maxillary region. The bleeding was stopped and the wound closed with suture at the hospital. The facial wound healed satisfactorily and the Plaintiff was discharged on 3 April 2000.
source: Multiple facial lacerations with active bleeding over the left maxillary region. The bleeding was stopped and the wound closed with suture at the hospital. The facial wound healed satisfactorily and the Plaintiff was discharged on 3 April 2000.

injuries.description: Moderate axonotmesis of the left infra-orbital nerve with facial sensory deficit; Professor Cheung awarded 2% permanent disability to the facial impairment from the scars and 1% permanent disability to the impairment of facial sensation.
source: When the Plaintiff was examined by his own medical expert Professor Lim Cheung on 18 January 2001, there was an obvious scar on the left ala of the nose extending into the nasolabial fold. The length of this scar was about 3 cm. A less conspicuous scar was also present over the left upper lip, extending laterally and crossed over the nasolabial fold. The horizontal and vertical segments of this scar were about 2.5 cm and 1 cm respectively. There was an area of facial sensory deficit located over the distribution of the left infra-orbital nerve and buccal nerve. The diagnosis was moderate axonotmesis of the left infra-orbital nerve. Professor Cheung awarded 2% permanent disability to the facial impairment from the scars and 1% permanent disability to the impairment of facial sensation.

injuries.description: One tooth in the left maxilla was loose, was extracted and a new dental bridge was re-made for rehabilitation of the Plaintiff's occlusion; Professor Cheung considered the loss rehabilitated and that no disability was justified.
source: About 10 days after the Plaintiff was discharged from hospital, he noted one tooth in the left maxilla was loose. He consulted a local dentist who extracted the tooth and re-made a new dental bridge for rehabilitation of the Plaintiffs occlusion.
According to Professor Cheung, the loss of the fractured tooth was rehabilitated by a new bridge and the chewing function restored. Hence, no disability was justified.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injury of hard dental tissues and pulp

injuries.description: Hearing impairment: audiogram on 4 May 2000 showed a sensorineural hearing loss of 50dB in the left ear; plaintiff's own expert considered subjective results unreliable and awarded 2.5-3.8% impairment of the whole person; joint expert found objective tests suggested a mild hearing loss above 2,000 Hz for both ears and concluded there was no permanent disability associated with hearing loss.
source: The Plaintiff complained of tinnitus and hearing impairment over his left ear after the accident. Examination conducted immediately after the accident revealed that his eardrums were intact and there was no other abnormal ENT finding.

Audiogram performed on 4 May 2000 however showed a sensorineural hearing loss of 50dB in the left ear. The Plaintiffs own medical expert Dr. Buddy Wong considered those results, which were based on subjective hearing tests, unreliable as the Plaintiffs eardrum was quite normal. Based on further objective hearing tests done, Dr. Wong concluded that the hearing loss in the left ear was mild or moderate (i.e. 30-40dB loss) and awarded 2.5-3.8% impairment of the whole person to the hearing loss.

The Plaintiff was later examined by the joint medical expert Dr. Lo Siu Sing on 4 February 2004. Dr. Lo also found the Plaintiffs response to be fairly inconsistent with the test results. Dr. Lo opined that the results from objective tests suggested the Plaintiff to be suffering from a mild hearing loss above 2,000 Hz for both ears. Since the Plaintiffs hearing thresholds were normal within speech frequencies, there was no permanent disability associated with hearing loss.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of middle or inner ear

injuries.description: Psychiatric condition: diagnosed as Post-traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) by Dr. Leung Chi-ming; plaintiff's expert Dr. Chung confirmed diagnosis and opined plaintiff was suffering from mild PTSD; joint medical expert Dr. Wong considered plaintiff to be malingering.
source: The Plaintiff complained of anxiety, persistent distressful re-experience of the accident, persistent avoidance of stimuli associated with the accident, depressed mood, lack of interest in activities, forgetfulness, insomnia and nightmares. He was diagnosed by Dr. Leung Chi-ming of Prince of Wales Hospital to be suffering from Post-traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD). The Plaintiffs own medical expert Dr. Chung See-yuen confirmed the diagnosis and opined that the Plaintiff was suffering from mild PTSD.
However, the joint medical expert Dr. Wong Chung-kwong disagreed with Dr. Chung and opined that the Plaintiff was malingering.

manifestations.description: Obvious scar on the left ala of the nose extending into the nasolabial fold; less conspicuous scar over left upper lip
Facial sensory deficit over the distribution of the left infra-orbital nerve and buccal nerve
Tooth loose in the left maxilla; extraction and placement of new dental bridge; chewing function restored
Tinnitus and hearing impairment; audiogram showed sensorineural hearing loss in the left ear; objective tests suggested mild hearing loss above 2,000 Hz

Anxiety, persistent distressful re-experience of the accident, avoidance of stimuli associated with the accident, depressed mood, lack of interest, forgetfulness, insomnia and nightmares (symptoms of PTSD)

treatments_future: continued psychiatric treatment for about one more year

losses.description: Obvious scar on the left ala of the nose and scar over left upper lip; facial wound healed satisfactorily but scarring present (length about 3 cm etc.)
Tinnitus and hearing impairment with sensorineural hearing loss in the left ear and mild hearing loss above 2,000 Hz on objective tests
Anxiety, persistent distressful re-experience, avoidance, depressed mood, forgetfulness, insomnia and nightmares associated with PTSD

The Plaintiff complained of anxiety, persistent distressful re-experience of the accident, persistent avoidance of stimuli associated with the accident, depressed mood, lack of interest in activities, forgetfulness, insomnia and nightmares. He was diagnosed by Dr. Leung Chi-ming of Prince of Wales Hospital to be suffering from Post-traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD). The Plaintiffs own medical expert Dr. Chung See-yuen confirmed the diagnosis and opined that the Plaintiff was suffering from mild PTSD. However, the joint medical expert Dr. Wong Chung-kwong disagreed with Dr. Chung and opined that the Plaintiff was malingering.
